title: Try something new for 30 days
speaker: Matt Cutts

keyTerms.definition: something you do regularly, often without thinking
a difficult task that tests you
able to continue for a long time
a long story in a book

predictionQuestion: Imagine you try something new every day for 30 days. What might change in your life?

keyIdeas.text: The idea: choose something you have always wanted to add to your life, and try it for the next 30 days.
He says 30 days is about the right time to add a new habit or drop an old one.
Lesson 1: the months became more memorable, instead of flying by and being forgotten.
Example: taking a photo every day for a month.
Lesson 2: as the challenges got bigger and harder, his self-confidence grew.
Examples: he started cycling to work, and he climbed Mt Kilimanjaro.
Lesson 3: if you want something badly enough, you can do anything for 30 days.
Example: he wrote a 50,000-word novel in a month (about 1,667 words a day). It was not very good, but he finished it.
Lesson 4: small, sustainable changes are more likely to stick than big, crazy challenges.
His final message: the next 30 days will pass anyway, so try something now.

modelNotes: - add sth new (or drop a habit, e.g. news) for 30 days
- 30 days ≈ right time for a habit
- 3. want it enough → can do anything for 30 days (novel: 50k words ≈ 1,667/day; bad but done)
- 4. small + sustainable → sticks; big + crazy = fun but ↓ likely to last (e.g. no sugar)
Message: 30 days pass anyway → try it now

questions.stem: Why does the speaker think 30 days is a good length of time?
options: It is about right for adding or removing a habit
It is short enough to forget quickly
It is the time between pay days
questions.answer: It is about right for adding or removing a habit
questions.explanation: He says 30 days turns out to be about the right amount of time to add or subtract a habit.

questions.stem: What was the first thing he noticed during his challenges?
questions.explanation: His first lesson was that the months were more memorable instead of flying by.

questions.stem: Which example shows that his self-confidence grew?
questions.explanation: He says he would never have been that adventurous before his challenges.

questions.stem: What does he say about the novel he wrote?
options: It isn't very good, but he finished it
He wrote it over a year
questions.answer: It isn't very good, but he finished it
questions.explanation: He jokes that the book is awful because he wrote it in a month, but now he can call himself a novelist.

questions.stem: Which kind of change does he say is most likely to last?
questions.explanation: His last lesson: small changes he could keep doing were more likely to stick. Big challenges are fun but less likely to last.
